claims.claim: Chiang argues that when an LLM fills in the choices a prompt did not make by averaging the choices other writers made, that average amounts to the least interesting choices available, which is why AI-generated text is often bland.
claims.source: Ted Chiang, essayist and SF writer, The New Yorker, 2024
claims.quote: that average is equivalent to the least interesting choices possible
claims.page: para. beginning "If an A.I. generates a ten-thousand-word story"
claims.routeHint: Wayback id_ capture 20260902201120 of the New Yorker URL; newyorker.com refuses direct WebFetch
claims.modelEra: ChatGPT-era LLMs unnamed beyond "ChatGPT"; observation published August 2024; register discussed is fiction (short story / novel)

claims.claim: Chiang argues that the alternative to averaging - instructing the program to mimic a specific writer's style - produces a highly derivative story rather than interesting art.
claims.source: Ted Chiang, essayist and SF writer, The New Yorker, 2024
claims.quote: which produces a highly derivative story
claims.page: para. beginning "If an A.I. generates a ten-thousand-word story"
claims.modelEra: ChatGPT-era, August 2024; register: fiction

claims.claim: Chiang states flatly that at the time of writing the fiction generated by large language models like ChatGPT is terrible.
claims.source: Ted Chiang, essayist and SF writer, The New Yorker, 2024
claims.quote: the fiction generated by large language models like ChatGPT is terrible
claims.page: para. beginning "Is there anything about art"
claims.modelEra: ChatGPT (unspecified version), August 2024; register: fiction

claims.feature: other: sentence-level choice as the locus of quality
claims.claim: Chiang argues that you could not replace every sentence of a thriller with a semantically equivalent one and have the novel remain as entertaining, so its sentences and the small-scale choices they represent determine its effectiveness.
claims.source: Ted Chiang, essayist and SF writer, The New Yorker, 2024
claims.quote: I doubt you could replace every sentence in a thriller
claims.page: para. beginning "Believing that inspiration outweighs everything else"
claims.modelEra: n/a - a claim about human craft, made August 2024; register: commercial thriller fiction

claims.claim: Chiang argues that ChatGPT has no more intention to communicate than a phone's auto-complete, and that this lack of intention means it is not actually using language.
claims.source: Ted Chiang, essayist and SF writer, The New Yorker, 2024
claims.quote: it has no more intention to communicate
claims.page: para. beginning "Some have claimed that large language models are not laundering"
claims.modelEra: ChatGPT, August 2024; register: general language use, not a measured corpus

claims.claim: Chiang argues that the selling point of generative AI - that it generates vastly more than the user puts in - is precisely what prevents these programs from being effective tools for artists.
claims.source: Ted Chiang, essayist and SF writer, The New Yorker, 2024
claims.quote: that is precisely what prevents them from being effective tools for artists
claims.page: para. beginning "It's harder to imagine a program"
claims.modelEra: ChatGPT / DALL-E era, August 2024; register: fiction and visual art

claims.claim: Chiang reports that Google pulled its Paris Olympics Gemini commercial, in which a father uses Gemini to compose his daughter's fan letter, after widespread backlash from viewers.
claims.source: Ted Chiang, essayist and SF writer, The New Yorker, 2024, reporting on the Google Gemini ad
claims.quote: Google pulled the commercial after widespread backlash from viewers
claims.page: para. beginning "Recently, Google aired a commercial"
claims.modelEra: Gemini, Paris Olympics (July-August 2024); register: a personal letter, not fiction

claims.claim: Preston reports that when a prospect asked several questions at once, the Brenda chatbot strung together a composite response that collated so much information she sounded hostile.
claims.source: Laura Preston, former chatbot operator, n+1 Issue 44, 2022
claims.quote: she sounded hostile
claims.modelEra: 'Brenda', a keyword-classification real-estate chatbot (NOT an LLM), observed 2019-2021, written up 2022; register: customer-service text messages

claims.feature: other: what a human editor fixes first
claims.claim: Preston reports that her standard intervention on Brenda's over-informative replies was to soften the aggressive recitation of facts with line breaks and merry affirmations.
claims.source: Laura Preston, former chatbot operator, n+1 Issue 44, 2022
claims.quote: aggressive recitation of facts with line breaks and merry affirmations
claims.modelEra: 'Brenda' keyword-classification chatbot, not an LLM; observed 2019-2021; register: customer-service text messages

claims.claim: Preston reports that Brenda's most common failure was errors of comprehension in which she would seize on the wrong keyword and queue up a non sequitur.
claims.source: Laura Preston, former chatbot operator, n+1 Issue 44, 2022
claims.quote: She would seize on the wrong keyword and queue up a non sequitur
claims.modelEra: 'Brenda' keyword-classification chatbot, not an LLM; observed 2019-2021; register: customer-service text messages

claims.claim: Preston reports that Brenda's developers touted her unrelenting consistency as a feature, claiming that because she said the same thing to everyone she was incapable of bias.
claims.source: Laura Preston, former chatbot operator, n+1 Issue 44, 2022, reporting the developers' claim
claims.quote: The developers touted her unrelenting consistency as a feature
claims.polarity: reports a vendor claim she disputes
claims.modelEra: 'Brenda' keyword-classification chatbot, not an LLM; observed 2019-2021; register: customer-service text messages

claims.claim: Preston reports that neither she nor Brenda could answer prospects' specific questions such as carpet or hardwood and which direction the windows faced, and that specifics were what people cared about most.
claims.source: Laura Preston, former chatbot operator, n+1 Issue 44, 2022
claims.quote: specifics, it turns out, were what people cared about the most
claims.modelEra: 'Brenda' keyword-classification chatbot, not an LLM; observed 2019-2021; register: customer-service text messages about places

claims.claim: Preston reports that when Brenda sounded odd and graceless, people were less likely to get intimate with her, which reduced the number of conversations escalated to a human.
claims.source: Laura Preston, former chatbot operator, n+1 Issue 44, 2022
claims.quote: when Brenda sounded odd and graceless, people were less likely to get intimate
claims.page: section beginning "Eventually I reached a level of virtuosity"
claims.modelEra: 'Brenda' keyword-classification chatbot, not an LLM; observed 2019-2021; register: customer-service text messages

claims.claim: nostalgebraist claims the main stylistic hallmark shared by DeepSeek-R1 and an unreleased OpenAI creative-writing model is the conjunction of one thing that is abstract or incorporeal with another that is concrete or sensory.
claims.source: nostalgebraist, blogger and ML researcher, Tumblr, March 2025
claims.quote: one thing that is abstract and/or incorporeal
claims.page: section "A mechanical boot, a human eye"
claims.routeHint: direct curl with browser UA on the tumblr.com permalink
claims.modelEra: DeepSeek-R1 and an unreleased OpenAI creative-writing model, March 2025; register: short literary fiction

claims.claim: nostalgebraist reports that R1 kept producing abstract/concrete conjunctions in spite of user-specified stylistic directions, including prompts to imitate named literary authors.
claims.source: nostalgebraist, blogger and ML researcher, Tumblr, March 2025
claims.quote: R1 even consistently does this in spite of user-specified stylistic directions
claims.page: section "A mechanical boot, a human eye"
claims.modelEra: DeepSeek-R1, March 2025; register: short literary fiction and author pastiche

claims.claim: nostalgebraist reports that the one pastiche free of the abstract/concrete tell was the Hemingway attempt, which he attributes to Hemingway having a distinctive and constrained style leaving no room for such flourishes.
claims.source: nostalgebraist, blogger and ML researcher, Tumblr, March 2025
claims.quote: presumably because Hemingway himself has a distinctive and constrained style
claims.page: section "A mechanical boot, a human eye", parenthesis after the pastiche list
claims.confidence: medium - nostalgebraist explicitly frames the explanation as a presumption, and judges that pastiche low-quality in other ways
claims.modelEra: DeepSeek-R1, March 2025; register: short literary fiction pastiche

claims.claim: nostalgebraist describes this crammed prose as having no modulation and no room to breathe, an unrelenting stream of gee-whiz effects.
claims.source: nostalgebraist, blogger and ML researcher, Tumblr, March 2025
claims.quote: no modulation, no room to breathe
claims.page: section "A mechanical boot, a human eye"
claims.modelEra: DeepSeek-R1 and an unreleased OpenAI creative-writing model, March 2025; register: short literary fiction

claims.claim: nostalgebraist guesses that the shared style of two unrelated models is convergent evolution, what happens if you optimize for human judgments of literary quality in a generic way.
claims.source: nostalgebraist, blogger and ML researcher, Tumblr, March 2025
claims.quote: maybe this is just what happens if you optimize for human judgments
claims.polarity: asserts as a guess about mechanism
claims.confidence: medium - the author labels it a guess ("I don't know why this happened, but if I had to guess")
claims.modelEra: DeepSeek-R1 and an unreleased OpenAI creative-writing model, March 2025; register: short literary fiction

claims.claim: Guo lists monotony as a tell, writing that in AI-generated content sentences are roughly the same length and the cadence never varies.
claims.source: Charlie Guo, Artificial Ignorance newsletter, 22 October 2025
claims.quote: Sentences are roughly the same length
claims.routeHint: direct curl with browser UA on the Substack post
claims.confidence: medium - Guo himself flags this tell as "more subjective"
claims.modelEra: ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini generally, named GPT-4o and GPT-5 elsewhere in the piece; October 2025; register: online prose, social posts, work email, long-form articles

claims.claim: Guo observes that LLMs uncommonly switch person or tense and tend to pick a lane and stay in it with unnatural consistency.
claims.source: Charlie Guo, Artificial Ignorance newsletter, 22 October 2025
claims.quote: They tend to pick a lane and stay in it
claims.confidence: medium - offered as the author's impression, no measurement given
claims.modelEra: unnamed contemporary LLMs; October 2025; register: creative writing contrasted with online prose

claims.claim: Guo argues that AI metaphors are plausible and generic, gesturing toward meaning without quite achieving it, whereas human metaphors are either highly specific or culturally resonant.
claims.source: Charlie Guo, Artificial Ignorance newsletter, 22 October 2025
claims.quote: They gesture toward meaning without quite achieving it
claims.modelEra: ChatGPT (metaphors he generated for a sample post); October 2025; register: short social-media-style prose

claims.quote: surface polish with nothing underneath
claims.modelEra: contemporary LLMs generally; October 2025; register: long-form articles and comments

claims.claim: Guo reports that a common AI failure is a paragraph saying in four sentences something that could easily have been said in one, with the other three adding nothing.

claims.quote: in four sentences something that could easily have been said

claims.claim: Guo argues that the it's-not-X-it's-Y parallelism is a legitimate rhetorical device but that AI uses it constantly and reflexively in situations where it adds nothing.

claims.quote: a good writer uses these devices sparingly, and with intention

claims.quote: to write things rooted in particular knowledge and tangible experience
claims.modelEra: contemporary LLMs generally; October 2025; register: long-form nonfiction
